clue.text: Highlander maybe in this cottage

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: the run of letters across these two words holds the Highlander

explanation.surface: A Highland crofter might well live in this little cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highlander is one example of a native of Scotland, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Mount beast of burden to cross river

indicators.note: the camel straddles the river, so the river's letter goes inside it

parts.note: a camel is a classic pack animal

explanation.surface: Someone climbs onto a pack animal to ford a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a verb about climbing aboard, but it names a mountain in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Carmel is a coastal mountain range in northern Israel, named in the Bible.

clue.text: Chief having mother at home

parts.note: ma is an everyday word for one's mother
someone who is in is at home

explanation.surface: The head of the household is the one whose mum stays at home.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief or principal thing is the main one, as in the main reason.

clue.text: Colourless opponents across the board

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lacking colour, monochrome, like an old film
second meaning: the two sides facing each other over a chessboard

explanation.walkthrough: 'Across the board' suggests 'everywhere'; here it is literally a chess or draughts board, whose pieces are the two colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Monochrome photographs and films are described this way, and the chess sides are named for their piece colours.

clue.text: Vessels carrying a group of sailors and birds

indicators.note: the bowls hold the other letters within them

parts.note: bowls are vessels for holding food, not ships
the article is used just as it stands
the Royal Navy, abbreviated RN

explanation.surface: Ships carry a naval crew along with some birds as passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' with 'sailors' close by suggests ships, but they are kitchen bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: These pale owls commonly nest in barns and farm buildings, which gives the species its name.

clue.text: Abysmal ignorance, hiding what is evil

indicators.note: the two words conceal the answer within their run of letters

parts.note: the tail of the first word and head of the second together spell the answer

explanation.surface: Profound ignorance is said to conceal something wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means harmful or wicked, as in a malign influence.

clue.text: Grey meal dished out sparingly

indicators.note: food dished out is served in pieces, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: these eight letters are the raw material for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A drab grey meal is served in stingy portions.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a scanty, stinting way is doing it with little to spare.

clue.text: In which a Gallic artist is found

indicators.note: the clue tells us the artist is contained in the words that follow

parts.note: the painter's name runs across the end of 'which', 'a' and the start of 'Gallic'

explanation.surface: A question about where a French painter can be found.
explanation.walkthrough: Marc Chagall was a Russian-French painter, so 'Gallic' fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc Chagall was a celebrated modernist painter known for dreamlike village scenes.

clue.text: Saw a little daughter taking long time

parts.note: the article is used just as it stands
little signals the short form, D
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: Someone observed a small girl taking ages over something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' reads as the past of see; here it is a noun meaning a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, a synonym for a traditional maxim.

clue.text: Athenian tiny boy getting on

parts.note: Tiny Tim is the sickly boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol
the word is used just as it stands

explanation.surface: A small Greek lad is making progress.
explanation.walkthrough: Timon of Athens is the title character of a Shakespeare play.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's misanthrope Timon is a citizen of ancient Athens, so he is an Athenian.

clue.text: Getting rid of a 19th century PM

definitions.meaning: second meaning: George ..., British Prime Minister briefly in 1827

explanation.walkthrough: To can someone is informal for firing them; George Canning died after only months as Prime Minister in 1827.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a present participle of sacking slang and the surname of a short-lived British premier.

clue.text: Old country fete to hold at one

indicators.note: the gala grips the other letters inside it

parts.note: a gala is a festive public celebration
taken as written
the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A village fete is to be held at one o'clock in an old-fashioned land.
explanation.definitionFit: Galatia was an ancient region of central Anatolia, home to the Galatians of St Paul's epistle.

clue.text: Girl initially found out complained

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word before is used

parts.note: only its opening letter is wanted here
to be rumbled is to have one's deception discovered

explanation.surface: A girl, once caught out, moaned about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Rumbled is British informal for exposed or found out.
explanation.definitionFit: To grumble is to moan or protest in a low-key, discontented way.

clue.text: Rubbish served up before work, a pancake

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish
to till is to work the soil
taken as written

explanation.surface: Junk food is put on the table before a job, and it is a pancake.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is a thin flat Mexican flatbread of maize or wheat, likened to a pancake.

clue.text: Grimace, catching cold in Bordeaux perhaps

indicators.note: the wine holds the cold letter inside, as if it had caught it

parts.note: Bordeaux is one example of a wine, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a face after catching a chill in a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: Bordeaux looks like the place; it stands for the wine from there.
explanation.definitionFit: To wince is to make a brief pained facial expression, a kind of grimace.

clue.text: Working for international organisation backed by the German

indicators.note: the first piece has the second standing behind it, coming after it

parts.note: the United Nations
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A man works for the United Nations with German support.
explanation.definitionFit: Working under someone means being subordinate to them, employed by and for them.

clue.text: Sarah and boy turned up in US city

indicators.note: in a down clue, both names are read from the bottom upward

parts.note: Sal is a pet form of Sarah
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A girl and a boy appear in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallas is a major city in Texas in the United States.

clue.text: Get rid of faulty tyres, do!

indicators.note: defective letters, so they are rearranged into the right order

parts.note: these seven letters are the raw material for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to scrap tyres that are defective.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy something is to wreck or eliminate it, ridding yourself of it completely.

clue.text: Teacher taking time to talk effusively

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish teacher of the law

explanation.surface: A teacher using the time to talk at length.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit on is British slang for chattering endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, to rabbit is to chatter on at length about trivial things.

clue.text: Target is hard — and optimistic

parts.note: the bull is the bullseye at the centre of a target
taken as written

explanation.surface: The goal is tough, yet someone remains hopeful.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullish describes a confident, upbeat outlook, originally of a rising stock market.

clue.text: Banker and bishop in row

indicators.note: the bishop's letter is placed inside the row

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats

explanation.surface: A financier and a churchman are having an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is a river, a thing with banks; 'row' looks like a quarrel but is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword convention makes a river something that has banks; the Tiber flows through Rome.

clue.text: This man's a mug

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a man's first name, as if pointing at a particular chap
second meaning: a ... jug, a drinking vessel moulded as a stout seated man

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like slang for a dupe, but it is a drinking vessel; the 's is just 'is' joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A Toby jug is a ceramic drinking vessel in the form of a stout man, and Toby is also a man's name.

clue.text: Explorer with gold standing up on ship

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: An explorer carrying gold stands upright on the deck of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: James Clark Ross was a British polar explorer, and the Ross Sea bears his name.
explanation.definitionFit: James Clark Ross charted much of Antarctica, so the surname names a famous explorer.

clue.text: Message this writer sent back — trouble

indicators.note: the writer's pronoun is turned around

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, so me
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.definitionFit: An email is an electronic message sent between computers.

clue.text: Cats wrecked site outside a B&B

a wrecked site is in disarray, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: these four letters are jumbled to make the outer part
the article is used just as it stands
bed and breakfast gives the two letters as they stand
